answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits show fabricated results or duplicate claims. Auditors are sampled from established participants and must also risk collateral, so collusion can be punished rather than treated as free voting power. This does not make Sybils impossible: an attacker can buy many identities, but must fund each one and risks losing the capital. Names like onyx, karst, and basalt can label audit cohorts, not serve as proof of identity.
